questions.cardText:
[Cultural Studies] In which of the following countries are Thursday and Friday considered the weekend?
A. Iran B. Vietnam C. Peru
Answer: A. In many Muslim-majority countries, the weekend is Thursday and Friday to align with the Islamic holy day of Friday. However, several have changed their weekend to Friday and Saturday or Saturday and Sunday to align more closely with international business practices.
questions.de: Welcher Wochentag, der Tag des Freitagsgebets (Dschumʿa), ist im Iran der Wochenendtag und in vielen mehrheitlich muslimischen Ländern der Kern des Wochenendes?
questions.en: Which day of the week, the day of the Jumu'ah congregational prayer, is the weekend day in Iran and the core of the weekend in many Muslim-majority countries?

timeline.labelEn: Saudi Arabia moves its weekend from Thursday–Friday to Friday–Saturday
timeline.labelDe: Saudi-Arabien verlegt sein Wochenende von Donnerstag–Freitag auf Freitag–Samstag

questions.notes: Card is dated/imprecise: Wikipedia says no country still observes a Thursday–Friday weekend; Iran's official weekend is Friday only, with Thursday a half day for public offices (many private firms take Thursday off). So the open question asks the underlying fact, Friday.

questions.cardText:
[Botany] What plant can live for thousands of years in the desert?
A. Welwitschia
B. Baobab trees
C. Cactus
Answer: A. The Welwitschia can live for over 1,000 years, surviving harsh desert conditions. It has only two leaves that grow continuously over its lifetime.
questions.de: Welche langlebige Wüstenpflanze Namibias und Angolas hat nur zwei Blätter, die ihr ganzes Leben lang weiterwachsen?
questions.en: Which long-lived desert plant of Namibia and Angola has only two leaves, which keep growing throughout its life?

timeline.labelEn: Friedrich Welwitsch documents the plant later named after him in Angola
timeline.labelDe: Friedrich Welwitsch dokumentiert in Angola die später nach ihm benannte Pflanze

questions.notes: Many plants are hundreds of years old, the oldest perhaps about 2,000 (Wikipedia). The open question keys on its two ever-growing leaves; the card says 'thousands of years' but its own explanation only claims over 1,000.
